references.text: Aaron refers to the tragedy that befell him on this day when his sons Nadab and Abihu died before the Lord.
Moses asked why the sin offering goat was not eaten, which Aaron answers here.
The law that the priest who presents the sin offering shall eat it in a holy place.
Aaron and his sons presented a sin offering and a burnt offering on this day, as Aaron mentions here.
Tithes and holy gifts were not to be eaten while mourning, which supports Aaron's argument that it would not please the Lord.
Hosea refers to the bread of the offering as bread of mourning, linking grief and holy meals together.
The Lord rejects offerings that do not come from a right heart, which reinforces Aaron's concern about what would please the Lord.
